---
title: "A line break before the parenthesis splits the call in two"
ref: SHY-01
categories: [Shiny]
impact: silencieux
attendu: "`rendered` holds the result of the call"
versions: "All"
source: "Slack ThinkR (2021)"
---

::: {.piege}
```{r}
compute <- function(expr) {
  paste("result:", expr)
}

rendered <- compute
({
  1 + 1
})

class(rendered)
```
:::

## Why

R reads one line and stops as soon as the expression is complete. `rendered <- compute` is complete: R assigns the function itself to `rendered`. The next line, `({ 1 + 1 })`, becomes a separate statement, evaluated and then printed.

In Shiny, the mistake looks like `output$chart <- renderPlot` followed on the next line by `({ ... })`. The output receives the `renderPlot` function instead of a render, and the code inside the braces runs once, outside any reactivity. The chart never shows up, and no error points to that line break.

## The remedy

Keep the opening parenthesis on the same line as the function name.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
rendered <- compute({
  1 + 1
})

rendered
```
:::
